clue.text: Immigrant wanting right remuneration

indicators.note: something wanting a thing lacks it, so the letter for right drops out of the immigrant word

parts.note: an incomer is a newcomer who has moved into an area

explanation.surface: A newly arrived worker is being paid less than they are owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is the money a person earns, a plain synonym for pay or salary.

clue.text: Water/G&T getting switched in wind up

indicators.note: the G in the water word is exchanged for the T, the second letter of G&T

parts.note: to irrigate land is to water it
the first letter of G&T, the gin-and-tonic abbreviation, is the one taken out
the second letter of G&T is the one put in

explanation.surface: Water or a gin and tonic gets swapped in, presumably to someone's annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: G&T looks like the drink, but it supplies the two letters to swap. To wind up is British slang for to tease or annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate someone is to annoy them, which is the British colloquial sense of wind up.

clue.text: Spooner's music adviser is a pest

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the opening sounds of the two pieces trade places

parts.note: rock is a genre of music
a coach is a trainer or adviser

explanation.surface: A music tutor is described as a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockroach is a scuttling insect that infests homes, a classic household pest.

clue.text: One's drunk painting in short skirt

indicators.note: the painting word sits inside the skirt word

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt
art is painting and similar works

explanation.surface: Someone has had too many and is painting while wearing a miniskirt.
explanation.walkthrough: One's drunk reads as a person being tipsy, but it means a thing that is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth, one example of a drink.

clue.text: Most importantly, a lovable rogue

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means behaving erratically, out of control, so these letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, these are the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A charming scoundrel is described, with the first phrase reading like an aside about his chief quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom used to stress the single most significant point.

clue.text: Corporate communication involved Tube line stress

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are tangled up

parts.note: taken as written, these are the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A company memo raises the strain of commuting on a London Underground line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A business letter is formal correspondence sent by a firm, a kind of corporate message.

clue.text: Former queen visiting museum gallery

indicators.note: someone visiting a place is inside it, so the queen goes inside the museum

parts.note: V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: The late queen tours a London museum's gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed open platform along a house, which can be called a gallery.

clue.text: Getting old and coping without servant

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the servant word is taken away

parts.note: managing means coping with a situation
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: An elderly person is getting by without domestic help.
explanation.definitionFit: Aging is the present participle of age, to grow older.

clue.text: Explanation on purpose

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket, the half of the field behind the batsman's legs
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Someone gives an explanation of something done deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is the key or caption on a map or chart that explains its symbols.

clue.text: What an anagram of "gathered" could be doing in passing

parts.note: read as the act of creating, what the rearranging does

indicators.note: this openly tells us to rearrange the next word

parts.note: taken as written, the word whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle-flavoured riddle asks what the reshuffled word is up to.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging the letters of gathered makes 'the grade', so what the anagram is doing is making the grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To make the grade is an idiom for reaching the required standard, as in passing an exam.

clue.text: Hamilton could be champion in expensive car?

indicators.note: the champion word sits inside the car abbreviation

parts.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the byword for a costly car
an ace is an expert or top performer

explanation.surface: Lewis Hamilton, Formula One champion, might be pictured behind the wheel of a pricey motor.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Hamilton is the British Formula One world champion; the question mark marks him as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is a motor-racing driver, so he is one example of someone who races cars.

clue.text: Interesting? Sailor's dreadfully boring!

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the crossword sailor, here with its possessive S

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is done badly, so the letters of boring are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the word whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a seaman is interesting and answers that he is terribly dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets interesting against boring, but the answer means the very opposite of the fodder word.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbing describes something so engaging it holds your full attention, a synonym of interesting.

clue.text: Ends spell in Italy

parts.note: a term is a period of time, as is a spell
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A sentence about finishing a period spent in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end points of a line or route, so the plural noun means ends.

clue.text: Time to get Harry in shape

indicators.note: the harrying word is placed inside the time word

parts.note: noon is a time of day, midday
to harry someone is to nag or pester them

explanation.surface: A trainer tells someone it is time to get Prince Harry into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like the prince's name, but it is the verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a plane figure with nine sides, one kind of geometric shape.

clue.text: Selling cars in business parks

parts.note: trading is buying and selling goods
an estate is a British name for a station wagon, a car with a long rear load space

explanation.surface: Car dealers are selling vehicles on industrial sites.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading estates are British areas of land set aside for factories and warehouses, the same as business parks.

clue.text: Honouring Lennon with big building

indicators.note: building means assembling, so the letters are put together afresh

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: John Lennon is commemorated with a large edifice.
explanation.walkthrough: Building looks like the noun for the edifice, but it is the verb, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennobling means raising to the peerage, or more broadly conferring honour and dignity.

clue.text: Cremation site witnessed up in the mountains

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of wood for burning a body

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: seen means witnessed

explanation.surface: A funeral pyre is spotted high in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are the range forming the border between France and Spain.

clue.text: Local diversion that involves pushing change at board level?

definitions.meaning: a local is a British pub, so this is a pub game
read literally: shoving a small coin along a flat wooden board

explanation.walkthrough: Board level sounds like company directors making changes, but the board is a game board and the change is a coin. The game is played in British pubs by shoving old halfpenny coins up a board.
explanation.definitionFit: This traditional pub game involves pushing coins into marked beds on a tabletop board.

clue.text: Settlement with grand English country house at the forefront

indicators.note: the country house is put in front of the other pieces

parts.note: a villa is a large country residence

explanation.surface: A settlement has a fine English manor at its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A village is a small rural community, one type of settlement.

clue.text: Lead quietly with change of decree

indicators.note: the letters of decree are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the word whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to lead softly after a ruling is altered.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede something is to go before it, which is to lead it.

clue.text: Rougher vintage claret served up

parts.note: a cru is a wine of a particular vineyard or quality

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the wine is read from bottom to top

parts.note: claret is a red wine

explanation.surface: A rather coarse old Bordeaux is brought to the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruder means more rough and unrefined, the comparative of crude.

clue.text: Socialist's standard warning

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the banner of socialism, and the name of the Labour anthem
second meaning: a signal of danger

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as a description of a socialist's warning, but the two senses are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarlet banner is the emblem of the left, and the same thing flown at a beach or racetrack signals danger.

clue.text: Party conflict? No way!

indicators.note: no means none of, so the road abbreviation is left out of the conflict word

parts.note: discord is strife or conflict
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to let a political group fall into infighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Party looks political, but it is the dance gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a social event with dancing to recorded music, a kind of party.

clue.text: Male singer embraces vibrato

indicators.note: the singer word holds the letter for male inside it, like arms around it

parts.note: a treble is a boy singer with a high voice

explanation.surface: A male vocalist uses a wavering pitch in his performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Male singer looks like one unit, but Male gives just its letter and the singer is the treble.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremble is a quivering, which is what vibrato is: a rapid wavering in a held note.

clue.text: Different pairs date differently

indicators.note: the letters are put together in another way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, these are the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Couples pick different times for their evenings out.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparate means essentially unlike, distinct in kind, a synonym of different.

clue.text: Former partner fronts French island bar

indicators.note: the former partner stands at the front of the island word

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or lover
ile is French for island

explanation.surface: An ex-partner runs a drinking bar on an island off France.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar looks like a pub, but it is the verb meaning ban.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them, barring them from their homeland.

clue.text: Started again with Reed in major championship? On the contrary

indicators.note: the surface puts Reed in the championship
this flips the order of putting, so the championship goes inside the name

parts.note: taken as written: Patrick Reed, the golfer
the Open is golf's oldest major

explanation.surface: Golfer Patrick Reed plays in a major golf event, and something resumed.
explanation.walkthrough: Patrick Reed is an American golfer; the Open is the British golf major. The clue's 'On the contrary' means the championship goes inside his name, not him inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reopened means opened again after closing, so it means resumed or started again.

clue.text: Lowers oneself, picking up people in Copenhagen

indicators.note: picking up a sound is hearing it, so the word is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: Copenhagen is the Danish capital, so its people are Danes

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to collecting Danish locals.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, to do something one thinks beneath one's dignity.
